papers.title: 3D bioprinting of a corneal stroma equivalent
papers.abstract: Corneal transplantation constitutes one of the leading treatments for severe cases of loss of corneal function. Due to its limitations, a concerted effort has been made by tissue engineers to produce functional, synthetic corneal prostheses as an alternative recourse. However, successful translation of these therapies into the clinic has not yet been accomplished. 3D bioprinting is an emerging technology that can be harnessed for the fabrication of biological tissue for clinical applications. We applied this to the area of corneal tissue engineering in order to fabricate corneal structures that resembled the structure of the native human corneal stroma using an existing 3D digital human corneal model and a suitable support structure. These were 3D bioprinted from an in-house collagen-based bio-ink containing encapsulated corneal keratocytes. Keratocytes exhibited high cell viability both at day 1 post-printing (>90%) and at day 7 (83%). We established 3D bio-printing to be a feasible method by which artificial corneal structures can be engineered.

papers.title: The Influence of Selective Laser Melting (SLM) Process Parameters on In-Vitro Cell Response
papers.abstract: The use of laser 3D printers is very perspective in the fabrication of solid and porous implants made of various polymers, metals, and its alloys. The Selective Laser Melting (SLM) process, in which consolidated powders are fully melted on each layer, gives the possibility of fabrication personalized implants based on the Computer Aid Design (CAD) model. During SLM fabrication on a 3D printer, depending on the system applied, there is a possibility for setting the amount of energy density (J/mm³) transferred to the consolidated powders, thus controlling its porosity, contact angle and roughness. In this study, we have controlled energy density in a range 8⁻45 J/mm³ delivered to titanium powder by setting various levels of laser power (25⁻45 W), exposure time (20⁻80 µs) and distance between exposure points (20⁻60 µm). The growing energy density within studied range increased from 63 to 90% and decreased from 31 to 13 µm samples density and Ra parameter, respectively. The surface energy 55⁻466 mN/m was achieved with contact angles in range 72⁻128° and 53⁻105° for water and formamide, respectively. The human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) adhesion after 4 h decreased with increasing energy density delivered during processing within each parameter group. The differences in cells proliferation were clearly seen after a 7-day incubation. We have observed that proliferation was decreasing with increasing density of energy delivered to the samples. This phenomenon was explained by chemical composition of oxide layers affecting surface energy and internal stresses. We have noticed that TiO₂, which is the main oxide of raw titanium powder, disintegrated during selective laser melting process and oxygen was transferred into metallic titanium. The typical for 3D printed parts post-processing methods such as chemical polishing in hydrofluoric (HF) or hydrofluoric/nitric (HF/HNO₃) acid solutions and thermal treatments were used to restore surface chemistry of raw powders and improve surface.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究SLM工艺参数对植入物表面细胞行为的影响。
summary_zh.method: 改变激光能量密度，测量密度、粗糙度、表面能及接触角，并观察hMSC粘附和增殖。
summary_zh.result: 能量密度增加提高密度、降低粗糙度，但抑制细胞粘附和增殖。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外细胞实验验证参数-表面-细胞响应关系。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how SLM process parameters influence surface properties and subsequent cell response for biomedical implants.
summary_en.method: Energy density was varied by adjusting laser power, exposure time, and point distance; density, roughness, contact angle, and surface energy were measured, and hMSC adhesion and proliferation were assessed.
summary_en.result: Higher energy density increased sample density from 63% to 90% and decreased roughness from 31 to 13 μm, but reduced cell adhesion and proliferation after 4 hours and 7 days, respectively.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture experiments with human mesenchymal stem cells were used to validate the biological response.

papers.title: Biodegradable Multifunctional Bioactive Glass-Based Nanocomposite Elastomers with Controlled Biomineralization Activity, Real-Time Bioimaging Tracking, and Decreased Inflammatory Response.
papers.abstract: Controlled biomineralization activity of biomaterials is rather important in bone regeneration and osseointegration avoiding the formation of fibrous capsule. However, most of conventional biodegradable elastomeric biomaterials for bone regeneration do not possess biomineralization ability and inherent multifunctional properties. Herein, we report a multifunctional bioactive glass (BG)-based hybrid poly(citrate-siloxane) (PCS) elastomer with intrinsical biomineralization activity and photoluminescent properties for potential bone tissue regeneration. Monodispersed BG nanoparticles (BGNs) were used to control the elastomeric behavior, biomineralization activity, photoluminescent ability, and osteogenic cellular response of PCS elastomers. BGNs significantly enhanced the elastomeric modulus of PCS from 20 to 200 MPa (10 times improvement) and the hydrophilicity (from 82° to 28° in water contact angle). The photoluminescent properties of PCS elastomers were also tailored through the incorporation of BGNs. The in vivo degradation of PCS-BGN nanocomposites could be efficiently tracked through noninvasively monitoring their fluorescent change. PCS-BGN nanocomposites enhanced the proliferation and osteoblastic differentiation of osteoblasts (MC3T3-E1) and decreased the in vivo inflammatory response. This study provided a novel tactics for designing the bioactive elastomeric biomaterials with multifunctional properties for bone regeneration medicine.

summary_en.motivation: To design biodegradable elastomers with intrinsic biomineralization activity and multifunctionality for bone tissue regeneration.
summary_en.method: Monodispersed bioactive glass nanoparticles were incorporated into poly(citrate-siloxane) elastomers to tailor mechanical, photoluminescent, and biological properties.
summary_en.result: The nanocomposites exhibited a tenfold increase in elastic modulus, enhanced osteoblast proliferation and differentiation, and decreased inflammatory response in vivo.
summary_en.validation: In vitro MC3T3-E1 cell assays and in vivo mouse model with noninvasive fluorescence tracking were performed.
